name: Question 2
problem: Given that $u=2x+1$, which integral is equivalent to $\int x\sqrt[3]{2x+1}\,\text{d}x?$
worked_solution:
Since $u=2x+1$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{1}{2}(u-1).$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt[3]{2x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{2}(u-1)(\sqrt[3]{u})(\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int (u-1)({u}^{1/3})\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int ({u}^{4/3}-{u}^{1/3})\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Given that u=2x+1, which integral is equivalent to ∫x2x+13dx?

a
−12∫(u4/3+u1/3)du
b
14∫(u4/3−u1/3)du
c
14∫(u1/3−u)du
d
12∫(u4/3+u1/3)du
e
12∫(u5/3−u2/3)du
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since u=2x+1, then we have dudx=2⟹dx=12du.

We also note that x=12(u−1).

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of u:

∫x2x+13dx=∫12(u−1)(u3)(12du)=14∫(u−1)(u1/3)du=14∫(u4/3−u1/3)du
